rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their rejection explains why God does not aid them: when signs were recited, they responded in three ways.
rows.anchor: لما بين فيما قبل أنه لا ينصر أولئك الكفار أتبعه بعلة ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase compares people far from truth to someone walking backward: they recoil from the signs and their reciter.
rows.anchor: مثل يضرب فيمن تباعد عن الحق كل التباعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes “in it” to mean the Kaʿba or sanctuary: they boasted that none could prevail over them because they were its custodians.
rows.anchor: إلى البيت العتيق أو الحرم كانوا يقولون لا يظهر علينا أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading takes the phrase to mean that they were arrogant in retreating and distancing themselves from the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: المراد مستكبرين بهذا التراجع والتباعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third analysis attaches the preposition to sāmiran: they gathered by night and slandered the Qurʾān as magic or poetry, insulted the Prophet, and spoke obscenely.
rows.anchor: تتعلق الباء بسامرا أي يسمرون بذكر القرآن وبالطعن فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sāmir can designate a gathered group, much as al-ḥāḍir does.
rows.anchor: والسامر نحو الحاضر في الإطلاق على الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage reports samran and sāmiran yahjurūn; yahjurūn may derive from obscene speech, while hijr can mean delirium or obscenity, or the verb can be emphatic.
rows.anchor: وقرىء سمرا وسامرا يهجرون من أهجر في منطقه إذا أفحش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They failed to reflect on a Qurʾān available for examination, eloquent beyond Arabic speech, free of contradiction, and pointing to God and divine unity.
rows.anchor: القول الذي هو القرآن كان معروفا لهم وقد مكنوا من التأمل فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier messengers brought miracles, with believers saved and rejecters destroyed; this history should have led them to believe.
rows.anchor: أن الرسل كانت تتواتر على الأمم وتظهر المعجزات عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They knew Muḥammad’s honesty and avoidance of lies before his prophetic claim; they had agreed to call him al-Amīn.
rows.anchor: عرفوا منه قبل ادعائه الرسالة كونه في نهاية الأمانة والصدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The madness charge was false: they knew him as the most intelligent, and a madman could not produce his decisive proofs and complete laws.
rows.anchor: كيف يمكنه أن يأتي بمثل ما أتى به من الدلائل القاطعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that they called him mad because he hoped for their obedience, which they thought exceedingly unlikely.
rows.anchor: كان يطمع في انقيادهم له وكان ذلك من أبعد الأمور عندهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another is that they called him mad to make ordinary people despise and refuse to follow him.
rows.anchor: قالوا ذلك إيهاما لعوامهم لكي لا ينقادوا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most hated truth because they clung to imitation and feared losing rank and leadership by accepting Muḥammad.
rows.anchor: لو أقروا بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم لزالت مناصبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some avoided faith from shame at their people’s reproach, not hatred of truth, as related of Abū Ṭālib.
rows.anchor: لا كراهة للحق كما حكى عن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The duty is to abandon desire and follow truth; if truth followed human desires, grave corruption would result.
rows.anchor: الواجب على المكلف أن يطرح الهوى ويتبع الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that the polytheists thought associating gods with God was true; that would corrupt the cosmos, as in the argument against multiple gods.
rows.anchor: القوم كانوا يرون أن الحق في اتخاذ آلهة مع الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that their desires were idol worship and denial of Muḥammad, sources of corruption; truth is Islam, and following them would require ending the world.
rows.anchor: أن أهواءهم في عبادة الأوثان وتكذيب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffāl says their opinions contradicted one another, so following them would cause contradiction and collapse the world’s order.
rows.anchor: آراءهم كانت متناقضة فلو اتبع الحق أهواءهم لوقع التناقض ولاختل نظام العالم عن القفال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Their reminder” can mean Qurʾān and proofs, or their honor and glory through the Messenger; these readings are close because Messenger and proofs establish one another.
rows.anchor: قيل إنه القرآن والأدلة وقيل بل شرفهم وفخرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is admonition and warning.
rows.anchor: وقيل الذكر هو الوعظ والتحذير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may mean the scripture they wished for, recalling their claim that they would be devoted servants if given a reminder from earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو الذي كانوا يتمنونه ويقولون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reading is bidhikrāhum, “their reminder.”
rows.anchor: لكنا عباد الله المخلصين } ( الصافات : 168 ، 169 ) وقرىء بذكراهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two occurrences have readings kharjan and kharājan.
rows.anchor: أم تسألهم خرجا فخراج ربك خير } وقرىء خراجا

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ defines kharj as a voluntary gift and kharāj as an obligatory payment.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمرو بن العلاء الخرج ما تبرعت به والخراج ما لزمك أداؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kharj is narrower than kharāj; the longer form suits the greater meaning.
rows.anchor: الخرج أخص من الخراج كقولك خراج القرية وخرج الكردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet asks no small payment for guiding people; God’s greater gift is better than anything people give.
rows.anchor: يعني أم تسألهم على هدايتهم قليلا من عطاء الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This refutes the suspicion that the Prophet seeks payment and shows the rejecters are without excuse.
rows.anchor: على أن هذه التهمة بعيدة عنه

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī argues no servant equals God’s provision; the phrase also implies servants provide for one another, or “best providers” would make no sense.
rows.anchor: قال الجبائي دل قوله تعالى : { وهو خير الرزقين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After exposing their position, God establishes the Messenger’s case: what proof establishes as sound is more fully straight than an ordinary road.
rows.anchor: زيف طريقة القوم أتبعه ببيان صحة ما جاء به الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who deny the afterlife turn aside from the path; uprightness is one path, while contrary paths are many.
rows.anchor: لأن طريق الاستقامة واحدة وما يخالفه فكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The harm from which they might be relieved can mean hunger and other worldly hardships.
rows.anchor: المراد ضرر الجوع وسائر مضار الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation is the harm of killing and captivity.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : المراد ضرر القتل والسبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation is the harm and punishment of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : أنه ضرر الآخرة وعذابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their rebellion is so entrenched that relief would not bring them back; if returned to worldly life, they would repeat what was forbidden.
rows.anchor: بلغوا في التمرد والعناد المبلغ الذي لا مرجع فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They would persist in error, wandering in confusion.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى لتمادوا في ضلالهم وهم متحيرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After God asks whether His signs were recited while they denied them, the condemned answer with two explanations.
rows.anchor: ذكروا ما يجري مجرى الجواب عنه وهو من وجهين

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf glosses “our wretchedness overcame us” as “our settled character overcame us,” like someone taking something from another.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : غلبت علينا ملكتنا

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf explains shaqāwa as an evil final outcome.
rows.anchor: قرىء : ( شقوتنا ) و ( شقاوتنا ) بفتح الشين وكسرها فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both shaqwatunā and shaqāwatunā are reported, with the initial consonant read with fatḥa or kasra.
rows.anchor: قرىء : ( شقوتنا ) و ( شقاوتنا ) بفتح الشين وكسرها فيهما

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim relates shaqwa to shaqāʾ, like jarya to flowing: the form can name a state, so here it means the condition of misery.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : الشقوة من الشقاء كجرية الماء

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says pursuit of forbidden pleasures and eagerness to do evil led to misery; they name the cause by its effect while admitting culpability, not offering an excuse.
rows.anchor: قال الجبائي : المراد أن طلبنا اللذات المحرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If choice arose without a cause, preference without cause would undermine proof of a Creator; if caused, its origin must be examined.
rows.anchor: فإن حصل باختيارهم فذلك الاختيار محدث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a servant’s choice needs a determining cause, another preference-maker entails regress; uncaused preference between possibilities is impossible.
rows.anchor: فإن توقف صدور تلك الإرادة عنها إلى مرجح آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A servant does not know the quantity or manner of actions and so cannot originate them; otherwise precise ordering would not establish divine knowledge.
rows.anchor: العبد لا يعلم كمية تلك الأفعال ولا كيفيتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People seek knowledge rather than ignorance; since even unbelievers intend knowledge but may become ignorant, God creates motives toward good or evil, producing felicity or wretchedness.
rows.anchor: فالكافر ما قصد إلا تحصيل العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If their alleged deviation were identical to denial, denial would explain itself circularly; deviation must be an antecedent cause, a created motive toward error.
rows.anchor: إن كان هو نفس ذلك التكذيب لزم تعليل الشيء بنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s command to be driven away and not speak affirms that disputation with God is impermissible and He is not questioned about His acts.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو صريح قولنا في أن المناظرة مع الله تعالى غير جائزة

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī says they had no excuse beyond confession; if they knew God created and willed their unbelief, they would more naturally cite it as an excuse.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي في قوله : { ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا } دلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī replies that their statement already gives that causal account, but they admit it does not excuse them; therefore God tells them to be silent.
rows.anchor: ولكنهم مقرون أن لا عذر لهم

none: The segment contains only quoted verse text, with no commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first clause has an omitted apodosis, possibly that they would have perished, been punished, or destroyed.
rows.anchor: أن جوابه محذوف وكأنه قال لهلكتم أو لعذبكم الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the address is to Ḥassān, Misṭaḥ, and Ḥamna, though it may be general.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس الخطاب لحسان ومسطح وحمنة

words: مَا زَكَىٰ مِنكُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ أَبَدًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis makes the apodosis the following statement that no one would ever have been purified.
rows.anchor: والثاني : جوابه في قوله : { زكى منكم من أحد أبدا }

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim proposes that indecency would spread and its harm become great without God’s favor and mercy.
rows.anchor: لكانت الفاحشة تشيع فتعظم المضرة وهو قول أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī prefers an omitted apodosis: intervening speech separates the later clause from the first. God preserved, delayed, and enabled repentance; in mercy He does not withhold what benefits a servant, even when that servant wrongs himself.
rows.anchor: والأقرب أن جوابه محذوف لأن قوله من بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khuṭuwāt is read with ḍamma on ṭāʾ or with it quiescent.
rows.anchor: قرىء خطوات بضم الطاء وسكونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khuṭuwāt is the plural of khuṭwah, from “to step”; the singular has an opening on its first letter, while the plural opens the first and dammas the second.
rows.anchor: فإذا أردت الواحدة قلت خطوة مفتوحة الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means the devil’s way and course: do not follow his traces or take his routes in listening to slander and spreading indecency among believers.
rows.anchor: لا تتبعوا آثار الشيطان ولا تسلكوا مسالكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although believers are specifically addressed, the ban applies to all accountable people, since everyone is forbidden to follow Satan’s steps.
rows.anchor: وإن خص بذلك المؤمنين فهو نهي لكل المكلفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional warning implies believers have not followed Satan; if the address meant unbelievers, they already had. God cautions believers after warning slanderers.
rows.anchor: وظاهر ذلك أنهم لم يتبعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faḥshāʾ is something whose ugliness is extreme.
rows.anchor: فإنه يأمر بالفحشاء والمنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Munkar is what people’s souls repudiate, recoil from, and do not approve.
rows.anchor: والمنكر ما تنكره النفوس فتنفر عنه ولا ترتضيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb and Ibn Muḥayṣin read mā zakkā with a doubled k.
rows.anchor: فقرأ يعقوب وابن محيصن ما زكى بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A zakī person has reached an approved level of obedience, like a crop that has matured; one is called purified only when actually pure.
rows.anchor: أن الزكي من بلغ في طاعة الله مبلغ الرضا

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: The author’s school argues tazkiya means producing purity in a subject, like blackening or reddening; the verse supports divine creation of purity.
rows.anchor: واحتج أصحابنا في مسألة المخلوق بقوله

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites interpret tazkiya either as performing acts of grace (luṭf) or judging a servant pure.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة ههنا تأويلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects the luṭf interpretation: if grace does not strengthen motive, it is irrelevant; if it does, its effect must be impossible, possible, or necessary.
rows.anchor: أن فعل اللطف هل يرجح الداعي أو لا يرجحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An impossible effect makes luṭf a deterrent; a merely possible effect occurs arbitrarily without a determinant; a necessary effect means God creates the servant’s act.
rows.anchor: فإن امتنع كان مانعا لا داعيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse attaches purification to God’s will, whereas performing luṭf is obligatory and cannot depend on discretionary will.
rows.anchor: علق التزكية على المشيئة وفعل اللطف واجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse calls purification grace and mercy, while creating acts of luṭf is obligatory, not discretionary favor.
rows.anchor: أنه علق التزكية على الفضل والرحمة

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The second Muʿtazilite reading treats tazkiya as God’s judgment that the servant is pure.
rows.anchor: وأما الوجه الثاني : وهو الحكم بكونه زكيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects that reading: declaring someone pure is obligatory when true, since otherwise God would lie; it cannot depend on will.
rows.anchor: فذلك واجب لأنه لو يحكم به لكان كذبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī concludes that the verse is explicit evidence for his school’s account of divine purification.
rows.anchor: فثبت أن قوله : { ولاكن الله يزكى من يشاء } نص في الباب

rows.speaker: كثير من المحققين
rows.claim: The phrase “in houses” requires an implied construction; many scholars supply “like a niche containing a lamp in houses.”
rows.anchor: أن التقدير كمشكاة فيها مصباح في بيوت أذن الله

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم بن بحر الأصفهاني
rows.claim: Abū Muslim objects that placing the lamp in God-approved houses adds nothing to the parable, since it does not make the lamp brighter.
rows.anchor: اعترض أبو مسلم بن بحر الأصفهاني عليه من وجهين : الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī answers that a lamp in clear glass placed in a mosque is grander and brighter, making the parable more complete.
rows.anchor: أن المصباح الموضوع في الزجاجة الصافية إذا كان في المساجد

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم بن بحر الأصفهاني
rows.claim: Abū Muslim’s second objection is that the niche, lamp, and glass are singular, whereas houses is plural, so one lamp cannot be in every house.
rows.anchor: أبو مسلم بن بحر الأصفهاني عليه من وجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī replies that the parable describes a type, so lamps of that description occur in all such houses and illuminate them at night for worship.
rows.anchor: لما كان القصد بالمثل هو الذي له هذا الوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second proposed attachment makes “in houses” modify the preceding phrase about being kindled from a blessed tree.
rows.anchor: التقدير توقد من شجرة مباركة في بيوت أذن الله

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم بن بحر الأصفهاني
rows.claim: Abū Muslim attaches the phrase to “an example of those who passed before you”: the earlier people are prophets and believers, and their houses are mosques.
rows.anchor: أبي مسلم أنه راجع إلى قوله : { ومثلا من الذين خلوا من قبلكم }

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم بن بحر الأصفهاني
rows.claim: On this reading, accounts of earlier prophets and believers identify their locations as prayer chambers, as in the accounts of the intruders and Zachariah.
rows.anchor: وقد اقتص الله أخبار الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام وذكر أماكنهم

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī objects that the earlier example concerns people who disbelieved and coerced slave girls into prostitution, not houses approved for remembrance.
rows.anchor: اعترض عليه القاضي من وجهين : الأول

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī also says this passage is disconnected from the earlier passage because the light verse intervenes.
rows.anchor: أن هذه الآية صارت منقطعة عن تلك الآية بما تخلل بينهما

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī treats this as a new sentence: the implied command is to pray in houses God authorized to be raised.
rows.anchor: قول الجبائي إنه كلام مستأنف لا تعلق له بما تقدم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj see no ellipsis, but fronting and delay: men of the described kind glorify God in the houses.
rows.anchor: قول الفراء والزجاج إنه لا حذف في الآية بل فيه تقديم وتأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection to al-Zajjāj’s order is that “in them” repeats “in houses”; Rāzī says added wording for emphasis is common and preferable to omission.
rows.anchor: قلنا الزيادة لأجل التأكيد كثيرة فكان المصير إليها أولى

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators identify the houses as mosques; ʿIkrima says they are all houses.
rows.anchor: أكثر المفسرين قالوا المراد من قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī prefers mosques: some houses cannot be described as divinely authorized to be raised, and remembrance and prayer aptly describe mosques.
rows.anchor: والأول أولى لوجهين : الأول : أن في البيوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view restricts the phrase to four mosques: the Kaʿba, Jerusalem sanctuary, Prophet’s mosque in Medina, and Qubāʾ.
rows.anchor: المراد أربع مساجد الكعبة بناها إبراهيم وإسمعيل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the house as the Jerusalem sanctuary, where ten thousand lamps are lit.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن هو بيت المقدس يسرج فيه عشرة آلاف قنديل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other view includes all mosques; Rāzī rejects limiting the verse to four without evidence.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أن المراد هو جميع المساجد والأول ضعيف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says mosques are God’s houses on earth and shine for heaven’s inhabitants as stars shine for earth’s inhabitants.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما المساجد بيوت الله في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that “raised” means built, supported by verses about raising the heavens and Abraham raising the House’s foundations; Ibn ʿAbbās says God ordered mosques built.
rows.anchor: المراد من رفعها بناؤها لقوله

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj interprets “raised” as honored and purified from impurities and idle speech.
rows.anchor: ترفع أي تعظم وتطهر عن الأنجاس وعن اللغو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The latter interpretation is preferable: the wording suggests houses existed before God authorized their raising.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني أولى لأن قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase covers every kind of remembrance, preferred because the wording is general.
rows.anchor: فالقول الأول : أنه عام في كل ذكر والثاني :

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets remembrance of God’s name in the houses as recitation of His Book.
rows.anchor: أن يتلى فيها كتابه عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation is that people should not speak there about what is improper.
rows.anchor: لا يتكلم فيها بما لا ينبغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr, from ʿĀṣim, read yusabbaḥu with fatḥa on bāʾ; others use kasra.
rows.anchor: بفتح الباء والباقون بكسرها

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: With the passive reading the statement continues through the time phrases; al-Zajjāj explains rijāl as the answer to “who glorifies in them?”
rows.anchor: مرفوع لأنه لما قال { يسبح له فيها }

rows.speaker: أكثرون
rows.claim: Most commentators understand this glorification as prayer.
rows.anchor: فالأكثرون حملوه على نفس الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take the prayer to be all five canonical prayers.
rows.anchor: فمنهم من حمله على كل الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the prayers as dawn and afternoon, said to be the initially required prayers before more were added.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من حمله على صلاتي الصبح والعصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes tasbīḥ as declaring God free of what is unfitting in His essence and acts; Rāzī finds it more apparent because prayer and zakat are separately coordinated with remembrance.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من حمله على التسبيح الذي هو تنزيه الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āṣāl is the plural of aṣīl, meaning late afternoon; ghuduw is a verbal noun and does not originally form a plural, while aṣīl is a collective noun.
rows.anchor: جميع أصيل وهو العشي وإنما وجد الغدو لأنه في الأصل مصدر

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf glosses bi-l-ghuduww as the times of morning, or mornings.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) بالغدو أي بأوقات الغدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant is wa-l-īṣāl, meaning entry into evening; āṣāl follows the pattern of aʿtum and aẓhur.
rows.anchor: وهو الدخول في الأصيل يقال آصال كأعتم وأظهر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the forenoon prayer is mentioned in God’s Book and recites this verse.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رحمهما الله إن صلاة الضحى لفي كتاب الله

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports from the Prophet that whoever regularly goes to the mosque, preferring it to other places, receives hospitality from God like that prepared in Paradise.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

rows.speaker: سهل بن سعد
rows.claim: Sahl ibn Saʿd reports a Prophetic saying that whoever goes to the mosque to teach or learn good is like a fighter returning with spoils.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية سهل بن سعد مرفوعا

words: رِجَالٌۭ لَّا تُلْهِيهِمْ تِجَٰرَةٌۭ وَلَا بَيْعٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says these men are not merchants or sellers at all.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم نفى كونهم تجارا وباعة أصلا

words: رِجَالٌۭ لَّا تُلْهِيهِمْ تِجَٰرَةٌۭ وَلَا بَيْعٌ
rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: The majority say they trade, but no commercial benefit distracts them from remembrance, prayer, or zakat.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم بل أثبتهم تجارا وباعة وبين أنهم مع ذلك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says they traded, but when God’s obligations came, nothing distracted them; they prayed and paid zakat.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن أما والله إن كانوا ليتجرون

rows.speaker: سالم
rows.claim: Sālim saw market people leave their sales and go to prayer, identifying them as those described in the verse.
rows.anchor: وعن سالم نظر إلى قوم من أهل السوق

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd is reported to have made the same observation about people leaving business for prayer.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود مثله ، واعلم أن هذا القول أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī prefers the view that they are traders: one says trade does not distract someone from a duty only when that person actually trades.
rows.anchor: أنه لا يقال إن فلانا لا تلهيه التجارة عن كيت وكيت
